question: In the middle of which century did the Arab traveller Sulaiman visit India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 9th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sulaiman al-Tajir (Sulaiman the Merchant) was an Arab trader/traveller who visited India and China and whose account forms the basis of the famous travelogue *Akhbar al-Sin wal Hind* (Accounts of China and India), compiled around 851 CE, i.e., the middle of the 9th century. (सुलेमान — 9वीं शताब्दी)

 

• He is regarded as one of the earliest Arab travellers to leave a written record of India, describing its trade, ports, and customs.

 

• His observations provide valuable information about the Pala and other contemporary Indian kingdoms and their maritime trade with the Arab world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later Arab travellers to India included Al-Masudi (10th century) and Al-Biruni (11th century), who accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni's expeditions.

 

NOTE

 

• 15th (Option 1): This period corresponds to travellers like Nicolo Conti and Abdur Razzaq, not Sulaiman.

 

• 11th (Option 3): This is the century associated with Al-Biruni's visit to India, not Sulaiman.

 

• 6th (Option 4): No such Arab travel account to India is dated to this century.

question: Ramnad V Raghavan is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mridangam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ramnad V. Raghavan was a renowned Indian classical percussionist known for his mastery over the Mridangam, the primary rhythm instrument of Carnatic music. (रामनाड वी. रघवन — मृदंगम)

 

• He was celebrated for his contribution to Carnatic percussion accompaniment and training generations of mridangam artists.

 

• The Mridangam is a double-headed drum, traditionally made of a hollowed-out jackfruit wood shell, central to South Indian classical (Carnatic) music concerts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known mridangam exponents include Palghat Mani Iyer and Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman.

 

NOTE

 

• Flute (Option 2): Associated with artists like Hariprasad Chaurasia and T.R. Mahalingam.

 

• Sitar (Option 3): Associated with artists like Ravi Shankar and Vilayat Khan.

 

• Sarod (Option 4): Associated with artists like Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian paddler who won a medal at the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)–Asian Table Tennis Union (ATTU) Asia Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manika Batra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manika Batra won the bronze medal at the ITTF-ATTU Asia Cup 2022, held in November 2022, becoming the first Indian paddler to win a medal at this tournament. (मानिका बत्रा — एशिया कप 2022 कांस्य पदक)

 

• She achieved this feat by defeating higher-ranked opponents, including a top-10 ranked player, en route to the semifinal.

 

• Manika Batra is one of India's leading table tennis players and was also the first Indian woman paddler to break into the top 25 of the ITTF world rankings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manika Batra has won multiple medals at the Commonwealth Games (including gold in singles at 2018 Gold Coast CWG) and represented India at the Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Mouma Das (Option 1): A senior Indian paddler and Arjuna Awardee, but did not win a medal at the Asia Cup 2022.

 

• Manti Ghosh (Option 3) and Naina Jaiswal (Option 4): Indian table tennis players, but neither won a medal at the Asia Cup 2022.

question: Padma Shri Award 2022 was given to whom among the following Kuchipudi dancers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padmaja Reddy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gaddam Padmaja Reddy, an acclaimed Kuchipudi dancer and Guru from Telangana, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 for her contribution to art (dance). (पद्मजा रेड्डी — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य, पद्म श्री 2022)

 

• She is credited with reviving the Kakatiyam dance form, inspired by the sculptures of the Kakatiya dynasty.

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the President of India for distinguished contribution in various fields.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Kuchipudi exponents honoured with Padma awards include Raja and Radha Reddy (Padma Vibhushan) and Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

NOTE

 

• Pallavi Krishnan (Option 1): A noted Mohiniyattam exponent, not associated with this specific 2022 Padma Shri for Kuchipudi.

 

• Sunanda Nair (Option 2): A Mohiniyattam and Bharatanatyam dancer, not the 2022 awardee referenced here.

 

• Sitara Devi (Option 4): A legendary Kathak dancer (Padma Vibhushan awardee, died 2014), unrelated to this Kuchipudi award.

question: The correct order of electron affinity of halogens is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is I<Br<F<Cl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom. Among halogens, the order of electron affinity is Cl > F > Br > I, i.e., in increasing order, I < Br < F < Cl. (इलेक्ट्रॉन बंधुता क्रम — Cl सर्वाधिक)

 

• Chlorine has the highest electron affinity among halogens, not fluorine, because fluorine's very small atomic size leads to high electron-electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell, making it comparatively less favourable to add another electron.

 

• Iodine has the lowest electron affinity among halogens because of its large atomic size, which results in weaker attraction of the added electron to the nucleus.

 

• This is a well-known exception to the general periodic trend, where electron affinity normally increases up a group; fluorine is the anomaly here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electron affinity generally increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group, with chlorine (349 kJ/mol) having the highest electron affinity of all elements.

 

NOTE

 

• F<I<Br<Cl (Option 1): Incorrect as it places iodine before bromine and doesn't reflect the actual order.

 

• I<Br<Cl<F (Option 2): Incorrect because it wrongly places fluorine, not chlorine, as having the highest electron affinity.

 

• I>Br>F<Cl (Option 4): Incorrect and internally inconsistent in the direction of the inequalities.

question: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under __________ of the Indian Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 21.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, which the Supreme Court has interpreted expansively to include the right to live with human dignity. (अनुच्छेद 21 — जीवन का अधिकार, मानवीय गरिमा)

 

• In landmark cases such as Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984), the Supreme Court held that the right to live with human dignity under Article 21 casts a duty on the State to ensure observance of social welfare and labour legislations enacted for workmen.

 

• This interpretation extends Article 21 beyond mere physical existence to include conditions necessary for a life of dignity, such as protection from exploitative labour practices.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21 has also been used to read in rights such as the right to a clean environment, livelihood, privacy, and speedy trial.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 17 (Option 1): Abolishes untouchability in any form.

 

• Article 15 (Option 2): Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

 

• Article 19 (Option 3): Guarantees six fundamental freedoms such as speech and expression, assembly, movement, etc.

question: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai, popularly known as "Punjab Kesari" (Lion of Punjab), died on 17 November 1928 due to injuries sustained during a lathi charge while leading a peaceful protest against the Simon Commission in Lahore. (लाला लाजपत राय — साइमन कमीशन विरोध, 1928)

 

• The Simon Commission (1928), an all-British committee set up to review India's constitutional progress, was boycotted across India with the slogan "Simon Go Back" since it had no Indian member.

 

• His death led Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Chandrashekhar Azad to assassinate British police officer J.P. Saunders in Lahore in 1928, as an act of retribution (the Lahore Conspiracy Case).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lala Lajpat Rai was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal) associated with the extremist phase of the freedom movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Lala Hardayal (Option 2): Founder of the Ghadar Party, not connected with the Simon Commission protest death.

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 3): Was inspired to avenge Lala Lajpat Rai's death but did not himself die in this protest; he was later hanged in 1931.

 

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Option 4): A prominent nationalist leader who died in 1920, before the Simon Commission arrived in India.

question: The estimation of poverty line in India is based on the survey conducted by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Statistical Office (NSO).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The estimation of the poverty line in India is based on data from the Household Consumer Expenditure Survey, conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO) (formerly the National Sample Survey Office - NSSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). (राष्ट्रीय सांख्यिकी कार्यालय — गरीबी रेखा आकलन)

 

• Poverty estimation committees such as the Tendulkar Committee and Rangarajan Committee used this NSO/NSSO consumption expenditure data to determine poverty lines.

 

• The NSO periodically conducts large-scale sample surveys on household consumption expenditure, which forms the statistical basis for computing the poverty line.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog is currently the nodal body for poverty-related policy matters in India, though the underlying survey data comes from the NSO.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 1): Handles fiscal policy and the Union Budget, not poverty line estimation surveys.

 

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 2): India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, not poverty estimation.

 

• Ministry of Rural Development (Option 3): Implements rural welfare schemes but does not conduct the underlying consumption expenditure survey used for poverty line estimation.

question:
Match the columns.

States: A) Bihar  B) Arunachal Pradesh  C) Assam  D) Goa

Cultural festivals: I) Bihu  II) Tam Ladu  III) Fatorpa Zatra  IV) Chhath
solution_text:
The correct answer is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bihar - Chhath (A-IV): Chhath Puja is a major folk festival of Bihar dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya. (छठ पूजा — बिहार)

 

• Arunachal Pradesh - Tamladu (B-II): Tamladu is celebrated by the Idu Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh to worship nature and seek protection from natural calamities.

 

• Assam - Bihu (C-I): Bihu is the most important cultural and harvest festival of Assam, celebrated thrice a year (Rongali/Bohag, Kati/Kongali, and Bhogali/Magh Bihu).

 

• Goa - Fatorpa Zatra (D-III): Fatorpa Zatra (also called Shri Saptakoteshwar Zatra) is a major fair/festival celebrated at Fatorpa village in Goa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable regional festivals include Onam (Kerala), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland), and Pongal (Tamil Nadu).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 present incorrect state-festival pairings that do not match the well-established associations listed above.

question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state in India has the highest share of limestone production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020 (published by the Indian Bureau of Mines), Rajasthan accounted for the highest share of limestone production in India, at around 29% of total national production. (राजस्थान — चूना पत्थर का सर्वाधिक उत्पादन)

 

• Chhattisgarh ranked second with about 17% share, followed by Madhya Pradesh with about 13% share.

 

• Limestone is a key raw material for the cement industry, and its distribution closely aligns with major cement-producing regions in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major limestone-producing states include Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Telangana.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1) and Chhattisgarh (Option 2): Notable limestone producers but with a smaller share than Rajasthan.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): A significant producer but ranks third by share, behind Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh.

question: As of March 2023 India men's Soccer team captain Sunil Chhetri became the __________ highest goal Scorer in International Football appearances.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sunil Chhetri, captain of the Indian men's football team, became the joint-fifth highest active international goal-scorer in the world in June 2022, and he continued to hold this position as of March 2023. (सुनील छेत्री — पांचवें सर्वोच्च अंतरराष्ट्रीय गोल स्कोरर)

 

• At that stage, only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Ali Daei, and Kunishige Kamamoto were ahead of him among top international goal-scorers among active and celebrated players.

 

• Chhetri had earlier, in June 2021, equalled and then surpassed Lionel Messi's international goal tally, drawing global attention to his achievement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhetri went on to become the joint-fourth highest international goal-scorer in June 2023, and retired from international football in June 2025 as India's all-time leading goal-scorer.

 

NOTE

 

• Tenth (Option 1) and Eighth (Option 2): Understate his position; he had already surpassed these ranks by March 2023.

 

• Fourth (Option 4): He reached this position only later, in June 2023, after the timeframe (March 2023) specified in the question.

question: The era of five year plans began in India with the establishment of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Planning Commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Planning Commission of India was established on 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet Resolution, and it launched India's First Five Year Plan (1951-1956), marking the beginning of the era of Five Year Plans. (योजना आयोग — पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं की शुरुआत)

 

• The Planning Commission was headed by the Prime Minister as its ex-officio Chairman and was responsible for formulating India's five year plans until it was replaced.

 

• The Planning Commission functioned as an extra-constitutional and non-statutory body, i.e., it was not created by the Constitution or by an Act of Parliament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on 1 January 2015, which does away with the five year plan model and instead formulates long-term policy vision documents.

 

NOTE

 

• The NITI Aayog (Option 1): Replaced the Planning Commission in 2015; it did not initiate the five year plan era.

 

• The Parliament (Option 2): India's legislative body; it did not itself establish or directly launch the five year plans.

 

• The Finance Commission (Option 3): A constitutional body dealing with Centre-State financial relations, unrelated to launching five year plans.

question: Which of the following principles was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in the Indian Constitution?
option_1: The State shall provide free and compulsory education
option_2: To organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines
option_3: To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife
option_4: Reservation of SC's and ST's in services
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 inserted Article 48A, a new Directive Principle of State Policy, which directs the State "to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country." (42वां संविधान संशोधन — अनुच्छेद 48A, पर्यावरण संरक्षण)

 

• The same amendment also added the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), including the duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment.

 

• The 42nd Amendment is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including changes to the Preamble (adding "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment also curtailed the power of judicial review and gave precedence to Directive Principles over some Fundamental Rights, provisions that were later modified by the 44th Amendment.

 

NOTE

 

• Free and compulsory education (Option 1): Originally Article 45 (DPSP); made a Fundamental Right under Article 21A by the 86th Amendment (2002), not the 42nd.

 

• Organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern lines (Option 2): This is Article 48, part of the original Constitution of 1950, not added by the 42nd Amendment.

 

• Reservation of SCs and STs in services (Option 4): Provided under Article 16(4), part of the original Constitution, not the 42nd Amendment.

question: In which months is Rabi crop sown?
solution_text:
The correct answer is October-December.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabi crops are sown in winter, typically between October and December, and are harvested in spring/summer (April-June). (रबी फसल — अक्टूबर-दिसंबर बुवाई)

 

• Major Rabi crops include wheat, barley, mustard, gram (chana), and peas, which require cool weather for growth and warmer weather for ripening/harvest.

 

• Rabi cultivation depends significantly on the moisture retained in the soil from the preceding monsoon (south-west monsoon) rains and on irrigation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharif crops (like rice, maize, cotton, jute) are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in September-October.

 

• Zaid crops are short-duration summer crops (like watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon) grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons (March-June).

 

NOTE

 

• April-May (Option 1): Corresponds broadly to the harvest time of Rabi or the sowing time of some Zaid crops, not Rabi sowing.

 

• February-March (Option 3): This is generally the harvesting period for many Rabi crops, not sowing.

 

• September-October (Option 4): This is the harvesting time for Kharif crops, not the sowing time for Rabi.

question: The periodic growth and drop of sea water level is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is tide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A tide is the periodic rise and fall of sea water level, caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on Earth's oceans, combined with Earth's rotation. (ज्वार-भाटा — समुद्र जल स्तर का आवधिक उतार-चढ़ाव)

 

• High tide occurs when sea water rises to its maximum level, and low tide when it recedes to its minimum level, typically occurring twice a day at most coastal locations.

 

• Spring tides (unusually high tides) occur during full moon and new moon when the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned, while neap tides (unusually low tides) occur during the first and last quarter phases of the moon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tides are important for navigation, fishing, and coastal ecosystems, and are also harnessed to generate tidal energy in some regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Wave (Option 1): A disturbance that moves along the surface of the sea, generally caused by wind, not the periodic gravitational rise and fall of water level.

 

• Sea current (Option 2): A continuous, directed movement of ocean water, generated by wind, the Coriolis effect, and differences in water density/temperature.

 

• Flood (Option 4): An overflow of water submerging normally dry land, unrelated to the regular periodic tidal cycle.

question: In which of the following years did the East India Company abolish the diarchy system of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1772.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dual Government (Diarchy) system in Bengal, introduced by Robert Clive in 1765, was abolished in 1772 by Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal. (द्वैध शासन प्रणाली — 1772 में समाप्त, वारेन हेस्टिंग्स)

 

• Under diarchy, the East India Company held the Diwani (revenue collection rights), while the Nizamat (administrative/judicial powers) remained nominally with the Nawab, leading to administrative confusion and exploitation.

 

• Warren Hastings ended this dual system and brought both revenue and administrative control directly under Company officials, moving the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warren Hastings also introduced significant judicial and administrative reforms, including setting up civil and criminal courts (Diwani Adalat and Faujdari Adalat) in Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• 1765 (Option 2): The year the diarchy system was introduced by Robert Clive after the Treaty of Allahabad, not abolished.

 

• 1757 (Option 3): The year of the Battle of Plassey, which established British political influence in Bengal.

 

• 1779 (Option 4): Not associated with the abolition of the Bengal diarchy system.

question: In India, which Ministry issues the coins of all denominations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Finance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, coins of all denominations are issued by the Government of India through the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs), under the authority of the Coinage Act, 2011. (वित्त मंत्रालय — सिक्कों का निर्गमन)

 

• Coins are minted at the four India Government Mints located at Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Noida.

 

• In contrast, currency notes (except the one-rupee note) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI); the one-rupee note is issued by the Ministry of Finance and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI manages the circulation and distribution of coins on behalf of the Government of India, even though it does not issue them.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of External Affairs (Option 1): Handles India's foreign relations, unrelated to currency/coin issuance.

 

• Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 2): Deals with internal security and administration, unrelated to coin issuance.

 

• Ministry of Mines (Option 3): Responsible for mineral resources and mining policy, not coin issuance.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about currency notes?

i. They do not have intrinsic value.

ii. They can be called fiat money.

iii. They are not legal tenders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement i is correct: Currency notes have no intrinsic (commodity) value of their own; their value comes from the trust and government backing behind them, not from the material (paper/polymer) they are made of. (मुद्रा नोट — कोई आंतरिक मूल्य नहीं, फिएट मुद्रा)

 

• Statement ii is correct: Currency notes are fiat money, meaning their value is established by government order/regulation, rather than being backed by a physical commodity like gold or silver.

 

• Statement iii is incorrect: Currency notes issued by the RBI/Government of India are legal tender, meaning they must be accepted for the payment of debts and other financial obligations within the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India moved away from the gold/silver standard system; today, the rupee is a fiat currency whose value is determined by the economy and monetary policy of the RBI.

 

NOTE

 

• Only ii (Option 1): Incomplete; ignores that statement i is also correct.

 

• Only i (Option 2): Incomplete; ignores that statement ii is also correct.

 

• Only ii and iii (Option 4): Incorrect because it wrongly includes statement iii, which is false since currency notes are indeed legal tender.

question: Net domestic product is calculated as______.
option_3: GDP – Net income earned from abroad
option_4: GNP – Net income earned from abroad
solution_text:
The correct answer is GDP – Depreciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net Domestic Product (NDP) is obtained by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from the Gross Domestic Product (GDP): NDP = GDP – Depreciation. (शुद्ध घरेलू उत्पाद — GDP घटा मूल्यह्रास)

 

• Depreciation refers to the wear and tear of capital assets (machinery, buildings, etc.) during the production process over a year.

 

• NDP thus reflects the actual net addition to a country's wealth after accounting for the capital consumed during production, giving a more accurate picture than GDP alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, Net National Product (NNP) = GNP – Depreciation, and National Income is generally equated with NNP at factor cost.

 

NOTE

 

• GNP – Depreciation (Option 2): This formula gives Net National Product (NNP), not Net Domestic Product.

 

• GDP – Net income earned from abroad (Option 3): Subtracting net income from abroad from GDP does not yield NDP; rather, GDP + Net income from abroad = GNP.

 

• GNP – Net income earned from abroad (Option 4): This computation actually yields GDP (since GNP = GDP + Net income from abroad), not NDP.

question: Which of the following claims concerning the magnetic lines of force inside a bar magnet is true?
option_2: From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet
option_3: Depends on the cross-sectional area of the bar magnet
option_4: From N-pole to S-pole of the magnet
solution_text:
The correct answer is From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Magnetic field lines of a bar magnet form closed continuous loops: outside the magnet, they travel from the North pole to the South pole, while inside the magnet, they travel from the South pole to the North pole, completing the loop. (चुंबकीय बल रेखाएं — चुंबक के अंदर S-ध्रुव से N-ध्रुव तक)

 

• This is a fundamental property of magnetic field lines: they never start or end abruptly; they always form closed loops, unlike electric field lines which begin and end on charges.

 

• The direction of a magnetic field line at any point gives the direction of the magnetic field (and the direction a north pole would move) at that point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The density of field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field — lines are denser near the poles, where the field is strongest.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not exist (Option 1): Incorrect; magnetic field lines do exist inside the magnet, completing the closed-loop pattern.

 

• Depends on cross-sectional area (Option 3): Incorrect; the existence and general direction of the field lines inside the magnet does not depend on the magnet's cross-sectional area.

 

• From N-pole to S-pole of the magnet (Option 4): This describes the direction outside the magnet, not inside it.

question: Which of these is a component of the tertiary sector of an economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hotels and restaurants.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The tertiary sector (service sector) of an economy comprises activities that provide services rather than producing tangible goods, such as trade, transport, banking, tourism, and hotels and restaurants. (तृतीयक क्षेत्र — होटल और रेस्तरां)

 

• This sector supports the primary and secondary sectors by providing essential services like marketing, distribution, and hospitality.

 

• The tertiary sector has become the largest contributor to India's GDP in recent decades, reflecting the country's shift towards a service-based economy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The primary sector involves extraction of natural resources (agriculture, mining, fishing), while the secondary sector involves manufacturing and industrial production (including utilities like electricity and water supply in the Indian National Industrial Classification).

 

NOTE

 

• Mining and quarrying (Option 1): Part of the primary sector, as it involves extraction of natural resources.

 

• Water supply (Option 2) and Electricity (Option 3): Classified under the secondary/industrial sector (utilities), as they involve production and supply of a physical output/commodity, not a pure service.

question: Which Asian country was the host of the first Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, from 4 to 11 March 1951. (प्रथम एशियाई खेल — नई दिल्ली, भारत, 1951)

 

• The idea of the Asian Games was conceived by Prof. Guru Dutt Sondhi, who was instrumental in establishing the Asian Games Federation (later the Olympic Council of Asia).

 

• A total of 11 countries participated in the inaugural edition, competing in 6 sports disciplines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice — in 1951 and again in 1982 (New Delhi).

 

NOTE

 

• Thailand (Option 1): Has hosted the Asian Games multiple times (e.g., 1966, 1970, 1978, 1998), but not the first edition.

 

• Indonesia (Option 2): Hosted the Asian Games in 1962 and 2018, not the first edition.

 

• Japan (Option 4): Hosted the Asian Games in 1958 (Tokyo) and 1994 (Hiroshima), not the first edition.

question: Sleeping sickness is a vector borne disease caused by the infection of which microscopic parasite of the species?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Trypanosoma brucei.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sleeping sickness (African trypanosomiasis) is a vector-borne parasitic disease caused by protozoan parasites of the species Trypanosoma brucei, transmitted through the bite of an infected tsetse fly. (निद्रा रोग — ट्रिपैनोसोमा ब्रूसी परजीवी)

 

• There are two main forms: Trypanosoma brucei gambiense (chronic form, found in West/Central Africa) and Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense (acute form, found in East/Southern Africa).

 

• Symptoms include fever, headaches, and, in later stages, disruption of the sleep cycle and neurological damage, giving the disease its name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sleeping sickness is one of several Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs) that the WHO has targeted for elimination.

 

NOTE

 

• Balantioides coli (Option 2): A protozoan parasite causing Balantidiasis, a gastrointestinal infection, not sleeping sickness.

 

• Giardia duodenalis (Option 3): Causes Giardiasis, a waterborne intestinal infection.

 

• Cyclospora cayetanensis (Option 4): Causes Cyclosporiasis, a foodborne/waterborne intestinal illness, unrelated to sleeping sickness.

question: The Chari Folk dance is primarily performed by women of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chari folk dance is primarily performed by women of Rajasthan, particularly associated with the Gujar/Saini communities of the Kishangarh region (Ajmer district). (चारी लोक नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• In this dance, performers balance brass pots (charis), often with lit lamps/burning cotton wicks soaked in oil, on their heads while dancing gracefully.

 

• It is traditionally performed on festive and auspicious occasions, symbolising the importance of water in the arid region of Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan is also known for other folk dances such as Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Terah Taali.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Ghumura and Dalkhai, not Chari.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for dances like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Chari.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Chhau and Karma, not Chari.

question: In 2023, the Government of India launched the nationwide 'Sarva Dawa Sevan' or mass drug administration to eliminate the disease __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is lymphatic filariasis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India, under the National Filaria Elimination Programme (NFEP), conducts the nationwide 'Sarva Dawa Sevan' (mass drug administration, MDA) campaign to eliminate lymphatic filariasis (commonly known as elephantiasis). (सर्व दवा सेवन — लसीका फाइलेरिया उन्मूलन)

 

• Lymphatic filariasis is a mosquito-borne parasitic disease caused by thread-like filarial worms, and India has set a target of eliminating it, in line with the WHO's global elimination goal.

 

• Under the MDA rounds, a combination of drugs (such as DEC and Albendazole, or the triple-drug regimen IDA — Ivermectin, DEC, Albendazole) is administered to the at-risk population in endemic districts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India aims to eliminate lymphatic filariasis as a public health problem, in line with the WHO's global target under its Neglected Tropical Diseases roadmap.

 

NOTE

 

• Thalassemia (Option 2): A genetic blood disorder, addressed through screening and management programmes, not through Sarva Dawa Sevan.

 

• Zika virus (Option 3): A mosquito-borne viral disease managed through vector control and surveillance, not mass drug administration.

 

• Multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (Option 4): Addressed under the National TB Elimination Programme, not the Sarva Dawa Sevan campaign.
